title: GPU demand bucketed weekly rollup (cluster & pool)
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is a weekly exported rollup that buckets incoming GPU demand signals by latency class and maps them to clusters/pools to estimate short-term headroom and recommended burst actions. Intended for on-call infra, capacity planning sync, and the Dedicated sales POV for burst guarantees.

Summary (high level):
- Week window: 2026-04-20 -> 2026-04-26
- Primary signal sources: realtime API queue depth, scheduled batch jobs, Dedicated pool prewarm traces
- New approach: bucket requests into three demand types (latency-critical, interactive, batch) and estimate peak GPU-hours per bucket per cluster to prioritize allocation and preemption policies.

How this was generated:
- Dashboard scrape of per-cluster 1h and 5m percentiles (P50, P95) for GPU utilization and active containers.
- Demand inferred from request arrival *estimated tokens-per-request* for transform workloads; batch jobs counted by job runtime * GPU count.
- We then map inferred demand onto current pool placement rules and quantize into 1-GPU headroom units for actionable decisions.
- Export columns below are the minimal set needed for weekly capacity triage.

Key definitions:
- Latency-critical: requests that target <150ms server-side latency (mapped to low-latency pools).
- Interactive: chat/generation work with soft latency bounds (150-800ms).
- Batch: offline jobs that tolerate >800ms but require sustained GPU-hours.
- Headroom GPUs Needed: integer GPUs to add to pool to meet 95th percentile demand assuming 70% per-GPU target throughput.

2026-04-26,apac,cluster-ap-1,lowlatency-p1,H100-80GB,72,97,35,70,460,8,latency-critical,planned spike from wholesale partner test

Aggregates (week):
- Total estimated GPU-hours across all buckets: 5,200 GPU-hrs
- Latency-critical share: 38% (~1,976 GPU-hrs)
- Interactive: 32% (~1,664 GPU-hrs)
- Batch: 30% (~1,560 GPU-hrs)
- 95th-percentile headroom demand (sum of HeadroomGPUsNeeded): 23 GPUs across regions

Notable findings / anomalies:
1) Cluster cluster-na-a shows repeated short-duration P95 spikes (2x background) during 14:00-16:00 PST which correlate to a specific job type (open PR: ops#412) that is bursty but short. Recommend: route those jobs into burst pool with preemptible instances instead of inflating lowlatency pool.
2) cluster-eu-1 has slot fragmentation in costopt-p4 causing effective utilization to appear lower while tail latency increases for interactive jobs. Repacking suggestion: allow 1h co-location windows and a small (4 GPU) compaction job to defragment.
3) apac cluster test on 2026-04-26 will likely breach headroom by ~4 GPUs; schedule prewarm or enable burst to partner-dedicated cluster for that window.

Recommendations and action items (owner tags):
- Short term (next 7 days):
  - Provision 10 preemptible GPUs in us-west as a temporary burst buffer (Owner: Liam O'Connor).
  - Create a scheduler rule to route PR ops#412 job class to batch-p3 for durations <90s (Owner: Maya Chen).
- Medium term (2-6 weeks):
  - Implement a demand-bucket routing policy in the router that tags requests at ingress (latency hint) so pools can be auto-selected (Owner: Eng Platform).
  - Run weekly compaction jobs on cluster-eu-1 to reduce fragmentation (Owner: Diego Ruiz).
- Measurement: Enable a new P99 latency metric per-pool for next two weeks and dump to s3 for offline analysis.

Open questions / risks:
- How do we reconcile token-estimation errors for multimodal jobs (images + text) that inflate inferred GPU-hrs? Suggest instrumenting token counts and job size at ingress.
- Dedicated customers may expect a stronger SLA for burst — what is acceptable for preemptible vs reserved burst? Raise with product-sales.

Notes to on-call:
- If a lowlatency pool P95 rises above 95% for more than 30 minutes, flip the "burst-mode" flag in the console for that pool (procedure: Confluence link in linked_artifacts).
- Use the attached compact CSV (exported) to compute immediate rebalances.
